issue: MCP server still writes backend/features.json directly via writeFileSync — violates ADR-007 invariant #3 (single write path across processes: MCP servers MUST call PATCH /api/featureflags/:key, not touch the file).
adr_quote: Single write path across processes. The MCP servers do not write the file directly. They call the backend REST API (PATCH /api/featureflags/:key) authenticated with a service token.
recommendation: Replace writeFeatures() with a thin HTTP client that PATCHes /api/featureflags/:key using a service token (MCP_BACKEND_TOKEN env). Keep readFeatures() either via GET /api/featureflags or accept the file-read for now (read-only path is not the race risk).
stage1_link: follow-up to ARCH-02 — ADR-007 was drafted in Stage1 but Stage2 fix-1 only addressed in-backend layering, not the MCP→file write path.

issue: featureFlagRoutes.js still performs its own read/write/validation against features.json instead of going through backend/utils/featureFlag.js — violates ADR-007 invariant #2 (single write path in process: all reads and writes go through backend/utils/featureFlag.js).
evidence: router.patch('/:key', ... { const data = await readFlags(res); ... await writeFile(tmp, ...); await rename(tmp, filePath); invalidateCache(); })
adr_quote: Single write path in process. Inside the backend Node process, all reads and writes go through backend/utils/featureFlag.js (extended to expose getAllFlags, updateFlag(key, patch), with cache invalidation on write). The route file becomes a thin controller.
recommendation: Extend backend/utils/featureFlag.js to expose getAllFlags(), updateFlag(key, patch) with cache invalidation + atomic write + Zod schema. Reduce featureFlagRoutes.js to a controller (route → util call → JSON response). Currently the route has its own cache (lines 17-19) parallel to the cache in utils/featureFlag.js (lines 9-10) — two TTL caches for the same file in the same process.

issue: Duplicate in-process cache: backend/utils/featureFlag.js holds (cachedFlags, cacheTimestamp) with 5s TTL while backend/routes/featureFlagRoutes.js holds its own (cache.value, cache.expiresAt) with 5s TTL — same data, same TTL, two independent module-level singletons. A PATCH via the route only invalidates the route's cache; util cache stays stale for up to 5s.
evidence: utils/featureFlag.js: let cachedFlags = null; let cacheTimestamp = 0  vs  routes/featureFlagRoutes.js: let cache = { value: null, expiresAt: 0 }
adr_quote: Cache invalidation. Backend cache (5s TTL) is invalidated on every write.
recommendation: Collapse to a single cache inside utils/featureFlag.js; route's invalidateCache() should call util's invalidateCache(). Otherwise isFeatureEnabled() in controllers can return stale results for up to 5s after an admin PATCH — observable race.
stage1_link: new — Stage1 noted ARCH-06 generally but did not call out the duplicate-cache bug specifically.

issue: Integration logic (URL construction, fetch, timeout policy, status mapping, JSON parsing fallback) still lives inside the router handler — ADR-006 invariant #6 explicitly mandates extraction to backend/services/n8nClient.js. Stage2 fix-3 added auth + tightened timeout but did NOT extract the service module.
evidence: router.post('/feature-control', protect, admin, express.json({limit:'16kb'}), asyncHandler(async (req, res) => { const base = process.env.N8N_WEBHOOK_URL; ... upstream = await fetch(target, {...}) ...
adr_quote: Single integration point. Any future AutoPilot endpoint goes through the same proxy module (extracted as backend/services/n8nClient.js per ARCH-05) — not as ad-hoc fetches scattered across routes.
recommendation: Create backend/services/n8nClient.js exporting forwardToN8n(path, body, opts) handling env validation, URL join, fetch, timeout, error→status mapping. Router becomes ~5 lines: validate, call client, pipe response.
stage1_link: follow-up to ARCH-05 — Stage2 only fixed the auth gap (SEC-7), not the layering. ADR-006 now makes this an ADR-trackable invariant.

issue: Dual transport (stdio + StreamableHTTP) selected from the same code via MCP_TRANSPORT env. This is a real architectural decision (single binary deployed two ways, shared tool definitions, divergent auth surfaces) but has no ADR. CLAUDE.md mentions it operationally but the trade-offs (shared schema vs duplicated app boot, bearer auth only in HTTP, session lifecycle differences) are not captured.
evidence: const mode = process.env.MCP_TRANSPORT || (process.argv.includes('--http') || process.argv.includes('--sse') ? 'http' : 'stdio'); ((mode === 'http' || mode === 'sse') ? runHttp() : runStdio())
recommendation: Propose ADR-008 — Dual-transport MCP server (stdio + StreamableHTTP). Record: (a) decision to keep single createServer() factory shared between transports, (b) Bearer auth only applies to HTTP path, (c) sessionId-based transport pooling in HTTP runHttp(), (d) tunnel/Cloudflare exposure surface, (e) why not two separate binaries.

issue: HTTP transport wiring (express app, Bearer middleware, session-pool dict, /mcp POST/GET/DELETE handlers) lives inline in runHttp() alongside MCP tool definitions. The file mixes three concerns: MCP tool/resource registration, stdio transport, and a full Express HTTP server. 365 lines, ~5 distinct responsibilities — god-file pattern.
evidence: function createServer() { server.tool(...); server.tool(...); ... } async function runHttp() { const app = express(); app.use('/mcp', (req, res, next) => { /* Bearer auth */ }); app.post('/mcp', async (req, res) => { /* session pool */ ... }) }
recommendation: Split into: mcp-features/server.js (createServer + tools), mcp-features/transports/stdio.js, mcp-features/transports/http.js (express + Bearer middleware + session pool), mcp-features/index.js (mode select). Cross-references ADR-008 (proposed).
stage1_link: new — Stage1 ARCH-02 covered features.json layering only.

issue: Module-load side effects: dotenv.config() at line 11, process.exit(1) at line 16 if COHERE_API_KEY missing, Cohere/Qdrant client construction at lines 20-21. Importing the file (e.g. for tests) starts an env-validated boot. The chunker logic in ingest.js is correctly exported as buildChunks() — but index.js has no equivalent seam.
evidence: dotenv.config({ path: join(__dirname, '..', '.env') })\nif (!process.env.COHERE_API_KEY) { console.error(...); process.exit(1) }\nconst cohere = new CohereClient({ token: process.env.COHERE_API_KEY })
recommendation: Wrap boot logic in a main() that is only called when import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href. Construct clients lazily inside the tool handler, or expose a createRagServer({cohere, qdrant}) factory accepting injected clients (mirrors ingest.js buildChunks export pattern).
stage1_link: follow-up to ARCH-15 — confirmed still present; recommendation now concrete given the buildChunks() precedent.

issue: Ingest pipeline (main()) and the chunker (buildChunks) live in the same file. The chunker is correctly exported and unit-testable, but the Cohere/Qdrant client construction is inside main() — good — yet the COLLECTION, VECTOR_SIZE, BATCH_SIZE constants are shared with mcp-rag/index.js (COLLECTION = 'proshop_docs' duplicated at index.js:18). Drift risk if VECTOR_SIZE/embedding model changes.
evidence: ingest.js:128 const COLLECTION = 'proshop_docs' ; index.js:18 const COLLECTION = 'proshop_docs'
recommendation: Extract mcp-rag/config.js exporting COLLECTION, EMBEDDING_MODEL, VECTOR_SIZE. Import from both ingest.js and index.js. Otherwise a model swap (1024→1536 dim) requires editing two files; if only one is updated, ingest writes vectors of one dimension and search queries with another — silent runtime error.
stage1_link: new — Stage1 did not separate chunker boundary from index/ingest coupling.

issue: protect (lines 5-36) and optionalProtect (lines 47-59) duplicate the JWT-verify + User.findById('-password') logic. Drift already visible: protect throws on User.findById returning null (line 19-22), optionalProtect silently proceeds with req.user = null. Two different policies, one shared verifier.
evidence: protect: const decoded = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET); req.user = await User.findById(decoded.id).select('-password') ; optionalProtect: const decoded = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET); req.user = await User.findById(decoded.id).select('-password')
recommendation: Extract verifyAndLoadUser(token) -> { user, error }. protect throws on missing/invalid; optionalProtect swallows. Single canonical verification, two policy wrappers. Also lands the seam for ADR-003 future refresh-token work.
stage1_link: follow-up to ARCH-12 — confirmed unchanged after Stage2. Lowered to C3 because it is hygiene, not security.

issue: Feature-flag evaluation logic is duplicated in three places with drift risk: (1) frontend hook useFeatureEnabled (Math.random bucket, Testing-only check), (2) backend isFeatureEnabled in utils/featureFlag.js (isAdmin bypass on Testing), (3) MCP set_feature_state status→traffic_percentage transition logic in mcp-features/index.js lines 152-157. Each implements the 'Testing fallback to 10' and the Enabled/Disabled→100/0 rules independently.
evidence: useFeatureEnabled.js:23 if (flag.status === 'Enabled') return true ... ; utils/featureFlag.js:34 if (flag.status === 'Enabled') return true ; mcp-features/index.js:152 if (state === 'Disabled') feature.traffic_percentage = 0; else if (state === 'Enabled') feature.traffic_percentage = 100; else { const tp = ...; feature.traffic_percentage = (tp >= 1 && tp <= 99) ? tp : 10 } ; featureFlagRoutes.js:75 same logic again ; featureFlagActions.js:45 same logic again on optimistic update
adr_quote: Schema. A Zod schema (in backend/utils/featureFlag.js) defines the shape of a flag. Both the REST PATCH validator and the MCP tool input validator import the schema. No more drift between MCP set_feature_state and REST PATCH.
recommendation: Centralise evaluation in a shared spec (could be JSON schema + a tiny pure-fn package, or document the canonical state machine in ADR-007 and reference it from each implementation). At minimum, lift the status→traffic transition rule into backend/utils/featureFlag.js and call it from both featureFlagRoutes.js PATCH and MCP set_feature_state (per ADR-007 anyway, since MCP should go through REST).
stage1_link: follow-up to ARCH-16 — extended with frontend hook and Redux optimistic update as drift sites.

issue: Reducer performs JSON.stringify(state.flags) === JSON.stringify(merged) deep-equality on every FEATURE_FLAGS_SUCCESS. This is a side-effect of the polling/silent-reload approach (App.js dispatches loadFeatureFlags on mount and presumably on focus). Two issues: (a) JSON.stringify on flags array is O(n*k) per fetch — acceptable at 10 flags, dubious at scale; (b) stringify-equality is fragile to key-order changes from the server. ADR-002 chose Redux with thunks and tolerates this, but the pattern hints that a server-state library (RTK Query, the deferred direction in ADR-002 'Current Assessment') would handle this natively.
recommendation: Either (a) accept and document — this is small-data, low-frequency, fine; or (b) when the v3.0 RTK-Query migration lands (per ADR-002 Current Assessment), feature flags is the canonical 'server cache' use case and should be one of the first slices migrated. No code change recommended now; flag for the RTK-Query migration ticket.
stage1_link: new — frontend was out of scope in Stage1 except for high-level ADR cross-ref.
